items.passage: In a long-running experiment, twelve initially identical populations of the bacterium Escherichia coli evolved for more than 30,000 generations before one gained the ability to feed on citrate. When Zachary Blount and colleagues replayed that population’s evolution from frozen samples, only cells taken from later generations evolved the trait, suggesting that it was ______ a mutation that had arisen earlier.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be predicated on something is to depend on it as a basis. When evolution was replayed, “only cells taken from later generations evolved the trait,” which means something that happened earlier in that population had to be in place first: the trait depended on “a mutation that had arisen earlier.”

A.why_wrong: Concomitant with means happening at the same time as. The text says the mutation “had arisen earlier” and that only cells from later generations evolved the trait, so the two did not occur together; the trait depended on the mutation.

B.why_wrong: Tantamount to means equivalent to. Nothing suggests that the ability to feed on citrate was the same thing as the earlier mutation; the replays show only that the trait could arise once that mutation was present.

D.why_wrong: Inimical to means harmful to or opposed to. The earlier mutation did not work against the trait: the trait appeared only in cells from generations that came after it.

band7_moves: consequence is the only clue (later cells only, so an earlier precondition)
academic word + preposition key
near-miss distractor naming the wrong relation (concomitant with)
all four options past rank 10,000

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Blount, Borland and Lenski 2008 (PNAS): twelve initially identical populations founded in 1988; no population evolved citrate use for over 30,000 generations; replays from frozen samples produced Cit+ only from later clones, so its evolution was contingent on a potentiating mutation that arose by 20,000 generations

items.notes: Subject: natural science (experimental evolution). Key letter C. Steps: 2 (only later cells could evolve the trait, so an earlier change was a precondition; then the rare word for depending on a precondition). Concessive frame: no. Transferred-sense key: no. Raw freq.txt ranks: concomitant with 44,623; tantamount to 33,899; predicated on 51,936; inimical to 27,949 (4 of 4 past 10,000; mean log10 4.59). Band-5 guard: clear (distractors as rare as the key). Near miss: concomitant with (a relation in time, not dependence). The source abstract uses “contingent”; the key is a different word and the passage uses neither. Lenski's name and the famous long-term experiment are kept out of the opener; the item rests on the 2008 replay study.

band7.why: Raw ranks concomitant with 44,623; tantamount to 33,899; predicated on 51,936; inimical to 27,949: 4 of 4 past 10,000, mean log 4.59, key past 20,000 (combined gate passes); rarest distractor 44,623 just short of check 2. Two-step consequence clue (only later cells evolved the trait, so an earlier precondition), as in 5e57efec; near miss concomitant with fails on the relation (time, not dependence); key never echoes the passage.

items.passage: Economists Ran Abramitzky, Leah Boustan, and colleagues found that sons of immigrants to the United States, both a century ago and today, have typically risen further up the income ladder than sons of US-born fathers with similar incomes. This advantage is partly ______ where immigrants chose to live: they tended to settle in places offering better prospects for their children.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Something ascribable to a cause can be attributed to, or explained by, it. The text says immigrants “tended to settle in places offering better prospects for their children,” which is offered as a reason their sons rose further; so part of the sons’ advantage can be attributed to where their families chose to live.

B.why_wrong: Tangential to means only slightly related to. The colon clause presents where immigrants settled as a reason for the advantage, so the two are closely connected, not barely related.

C.why_wrong: Impervious to means unaffected by. The colon clause explains the advantage by where immigrants settled, so the advantage is affected by that choice, not unaffected by it.

D.why_wrong: Commensurate with means matching in size or degree. The text compares nothing in size with “where immigrants chose to live”; it says only that this choice helps explain the advantage.

band7_moves: academic word + preposition key that cannot be decoded at sight (ascribable, not traceable)
clue is a cause stated after a colon, in a plainer register than the key
near-miss distractor on degree of connection (tangential to)
all four options past rank 10,000

sources.what: AEA page for Abramitzky, Boustan, Jácome and Pérez, “Intergenerational Mobility of Immigrants in the United States over Two Centuries” (AER 2021): millions of father-son pairs; children of immigrants from nearly every sending country have higher upward mobility than children of the US-born, in historical and modern data; immigrants gain this advantage partly by choosing to settle in locations that offer better prospects for their children

items.notes: Subject: social science (economic history). Key letter A. Steps: 2 (the colon clause gives a cause; the blank must name the relation of an effect to its cause, and “partly” rules out a word meaning wholly determined). Concessive frame: no. Transferred-sense key: no. Raw freq.txt ranks (reviewer recount): ascribable to unseen (ascribe 27,367); tangential to unseen; impervious to 20,091; commensurate with 34,042 (4 of 4 past 10,000; mean log10 5.21). Reviewer changed the key from traceable to (29,428) and the near miss from incidental to: traceable is trace + able, which the stem lookup does not strip, so a student decodes it at sight and the rare distractors never come into play; ascribable cannot be decoded without knowing ascribe. contingent on was avoided because it already keys or appears in 8 of our WIC items. Detail kept to the abstract: the location-choice mechanism only.

band7.why: After the fix: ascribable to unseen (ascribe 27,367), tangential to unseen, impervious to 20,091, commensurate with 34,042: 4 of 4 past 10,000, mean log 5.21, two options unseen (check 2 passes). The draft key traceable to read band 6: it decodes at sight as trace + able, so the rare set never mattered. One-step cause clue after a colon, so the vocabulary carries the item, as in b411eb09 and 5ccbfe22; near miss tangential to on degree.

fixes: hardened for band 7: key traceable to (decodes at sight as trace + able) replaced by ascribable to; near miss incidental to replaced by tangential to; explanation, why_wrong and notes rewritten; re-solved blind, one defensible answer

items.passage: Since the late 1970s, deaf children in Nicaragua have collectively created a new sign language. Ann Senghas and colleagues found that its earliest signers ______ complex events into basic elements and then recombined those elements in sequences, a pattern absent from the gestures that hearing Nicaraguans produce while speaking Spanish.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To parse something is to break it into its component parts, as a sentence is broken into words. The text says the earliest signers broke complex events down “into basic elements” and then “recombined those elements in sequences,” so they parsed those events.

A.why_wrong: Conflated means merged into one. The signers did the opposite: they divided complex events “into basic elements.”

B.why_wrong: Transcribed means written down or copied into another form of writing. Nothing in the text involves writing; the signers broke events into elements of a sign language.

C.why_wrong: Sublimated means turned or redirected into a more refined form. The text describes events being divided into basic parts, not being transformed into something higher.

band7_moves: transferred-sense key (parse) in a plainer clue register
all four options past rank 10,000
reversal that names the gesture pattern the signers avoided (conflated)

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Senghas, Kita and Özyürek 2004 (Science): a new sign language created by deaf Nicaraguans over the past 25 years; in its initial creation children analyzed complex events into basic elements and sequenced these elements, by principles not observed in the gestures accompanying speech in the surrounding language; the abstract speaks of this early segmentation and recombination

items.notes: Subject: social science (linguistics). Key letter D. Steps: 2 (the frame “X into basic elements” plus the later recombining of those elements describes analysis into parts; the student must then know the transferred, grammatical sense of parse). Concessive frame: no. Transferred-sense key: yes (parse, from grammar, used of events). Raw freq.txt ranks: conflated unseen; transcribed 32,187; sublimated 36,897; parsed 53,653 (4 of 4 past 10,000; mean log10 4.95). Band-5 guard: clear. The source says “analyzed”; the passage avoids that word. “Since the late 1970s” follows the abstract's “over the past 25 years” (2004).

band7.why: Raw ranks conflated unseen; transcribed 32,187; sublimated 36,897; parsed 53,653: 4 of 4 past 10,000, mean log 4.95, key past 50,000. Key in a transferred sense (parse, from grammar, used of events), a band-7 move (5444db38, inertia); the clue (into basic elements) is plainer than the key; conflated is the reversal. One step, carried by vocabulary as in 93665100.

items.passage: Many models of obesity assume that sedentary Western lifestyles reduce daily energy expenditure, implying that the expenditure of physically active hunter-gatherers should be comparatively ______. Yet when Herman Pontzer and colleagues measured it among Hadza foragers in Tanzania, the adults burned roughly as many calories per day as Western adults, once differences in body size were accounted for.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: If sedentary Western lifestyles “reduce daily energy expenditure,” as the models assume, then active hunter-gatherers should burn more: their expenditure should be elevated, or raised. The “Yet” sentence reports that this expectation failed, since the Hadza adults “burned roughly as many calories per day as Western adults.”

A.recipe: reversal: trait of the other side (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Unremarkable describes what Pontzer and colleagues actually found, not what the models implied. The blank completes the expectation that the “Yet” sentence then contradicts.

C.why_wrong: Erratic means irregular or unpredictable. The models are described as predicting a difference in amount between lifestyles, not irregular expenditure from day to day.

D.why_wrong: Seasonal means changing with the seasons. Nothing in the text concerns seasons; the models’ implication is that active people burn more energy than sedentary ones.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Pontzer et al. 2012 (PLoS ONE): doubly labeled water in Hadza foragers; physical activity higher than among Westerners but average daily energy expenditure no different from Westerners' after controlling for body size; challenges models of obesity suggesting that Western lifestyles lead to decreased energy expenditure

items.notes: Subject: social science (biological anthropology). Key letter B. Band target 6 per plan. Steps: 2 (the models' premise that sedentary life lowers expenditure implies active foragers burn more; then the Yet sentence shows the blank holds the expectation, not the finding). The blank sits on the received view, and the finding's own trait (unremarkable) is offered as the trap. Raw freq.txt ranks: unremarkable 64,876; elevated 8,562; erratic 16,787; seasonal 45,224. Fame check: Hadza appear in live items on sleep, the endowment effect and footprints; this energy study is not used anywhere.

band7.why: Target 6 per plan and it meets it: B3 received view with the blank on the expectation and the finding (unremarkable) as the wrong-party trap, two steps, as b35e2fdc. The key elevated (8,562) is the commonest option, so it cannot be band 7 by vocabulary; a strong band 6.

items.passage: Borealopelta markmitchelli, an armored dinosaur unearthed in 2011 in a mine in Alberta, Canada, is so well preserved that pigment survives in its fossilized skin. Caleb Brown and colleagues found that the pigment forms a countershaded pattern, a form of camouflage, suggesting that the animal’s bulk and armor, however formidable, failed to ______ the need to hide from predators.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To obviate a need is to remove it or make it unnecessary. An animal with camouflage was hiding from something, so the countershading shows that Borealopelta still faced predators: its bulk and armor, “however formidable,” did not remove “the need to hide from predators.”

B.why_wrong: Precipitate means to bring about suddenly. Nothing in the text suggests that the animal’s bulk or armor might have caused the need to hide; the point is that they did not end that need.

C.why_wrong: Corroborate means to confirm with evidence. The pigment is the evidence in the text; the animal’s bulk and armor cannot confirm a need.

D.why_wrong: Aggravate means to make worse. The text never suggests that bulk or armor could increase the need to hide; it concerns whether they made hiding unnecessary.

band7_moves: negation hidden in a verb (failed to)
counterintuitive inference: armor did not remove the need to hide
three-step chain from pigment to predation to armor
all four options past rank 10,000, three plainly unsupported but rare

sources.what: Wikipedia, Borealopelta: found at Suncor's Millennium Mine, Alberta, March 2011; three-dimensional preservation with skin; pigment studies show reddish-brown coloration in a countershaded pattern used for camouflage (Brown et al. 2017), suggesting the animal was under threat of predation despite its large size

items.notes: Subject: natural science (paleontology). Key letter A. Steps: 3 (countershading is camouflage; camouflage means predators were a threat; so the animal's bulk and armor did not make hiding unnecessary, as the source says: under threat of predation despite its large size, armor primarily defensive). Negation hidden in a verb (failed to) as in d5ad34f0, with a counterintuitive point (a heavily armored animal still needed to hide). Concessive: yes (however formidable). Raw freq.txt ranks: obviate 33,787; precipitate 14,384; corroborate 34,984; aggravate 33,962 (4 of 4 past 10,000; mean log10 4.44). All three distractors are plainly unsupported but rare (the band-7 pattern in d5ad34f0 and d7807ec8); a near synonym such as mitigate was left out because “failed to mitigate” could be defended. The item hinges on armor despite predation, not on countershading as such (Psittacosaurus countershading is a live CID subject).

band7.why: Raw ranks obviate 33,787; precipitate 14,384; corroborate 34,984; aggravate 33,962: 4 of 4 past 10,000, mean log 4.44, key past 20,000. Negation hidden in a verb (failed to) as in d5ad34f0, a concessive (however formidable), and a three-step chain (countershading, so predators, so armor did not remove the need). Three rare unsupported distractors, the band-7 pattern of d7807ec8.

fixes: species epithet corrected from markleyi to markmitchelli (Wikipedia, Borealopelta: “It contains a single species, B. markmitchelli, named in 2017 by Caleb Brown and colleagues”)

items.passage: Nathan Nunn and Leonard Wantchekon found that Africans whose ancestors were most heavily raided during the slave trades tend to be less trusting of others today. Since this effect operates mainly through norms and beliefs internal to individuals, the mistrust has proved ______, outlasting the trades themselves by generations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Tenacious means holding firmly and lasting a long time. Because the mistrust is carried in “norms and beliefs internal to individuals,” it travels with people and is passed down, and the text says it is still present, “outlasting the trades themselves by generations.”

A.why_wrong: Mercurial means changeable and quick to shift. The text says the mistrust has lasted “by generations” beyond the slave trades, so it has been stable, not changeable.

B.why_wrong: Salutary means beneficial. The text reports that the slave trades left people less trusting of others; nothing presents this mistrust as good for them.

C.why_wrong: Insular means narrow or cut off from outside influence, a word sometimes used of attitudes. The sentence explains why the mistrust has lasted so long, and insular says nothing about lasting.

band7_moves: evaluative key in a cause frame (Since clause)
all four options past rank 10,000
near-miss distractor from the attitude family (insular)

sources.what: AEA page for Nunn and Wantchekon, “The Slave Trade and the Origins of Mistrust in Africa” (AER 2011): individuals whose ancestors were heavily raided during the slave trade are less trusting today; most of the impact of the slave trade is through factors internal to the individual, such as cultural norms, beliefs, and values

items.notes: Subject: social science (economics, history). Key letter D. Steps: 2 (norms held by individuals travel with them and pass down, so the mistrust lasts; the participle restates the lasting, and the student must know tenacious). Cause in a Since clause in the same sentence, as in 571cf537. Concessive frame: no. Raw freq.txt ranks: mercurial 30,270; salutary 23,342; insular 34,183; tenacious 15,769 (4 of 4 past 10,000; mean log10 4.40). Near miss: insular (a word for closed attitudes, but not for lasting). “Internal to individuals” follows the abstract's wording.

band7.why: Raw ranks mercurial 30,270; salutary 23,342; insular 34,183; tenacious 15,769: 4 of 4 past 10,000, mean log 4.40 (above the band-7 mean 4.28). B2 recipe as in 571cf537: an evaluative key in a Since clause, with the reversal (mercurial) and an attitude-family near miss (insular). The softest of the set: one step, the key is the commonest option and no distractor passes 50,000, so it sits at the 6/7 line; the option-set rarity decides it.

items.passage: During 1913 and 1914, British archaeologist and writer Gertrude Bell journeyed approximately 1,800 miles from Damascus to the Arabian settlement of Ha’il and onward to Baghdad. Only one foreign woman had previously ventured to Ha’il, and Bell was forcibly detained there for eleven days, so her expedition could hardly be considered ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Hardly routine means far from ordinary. The text gives two reasons the expedition was unusual: “Only one foreign woman had previously ventured to Ha’il,” and Bell “was forcibly detained there for eleven days.”

A.why_wrong: Saying the expedition could hardly be considered arduous would mean it was easy, but a trip of “approximately 1,800 miles” that included being detained for eleven days was clearly hard.

B.why_wrong: Lucrative means profitable. The text says nothing about money, so the reasons it gives do not bear on whether the expedition was profitable.

D.why_wrong: Ceremonial means formal or ritual. The text never suggests the expedition was a ceremony, and the reasons it gives concern how unusual the trip was.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Gertrude Bell: English writer, traveller and archaeologist; 1913–14 journey of about 1,800 miles from Damascus to Ha'il, then to Baghdad; only the second foreign woman to visit Ha'il, after Lady Anne Blunt; held prisoner there for eleven days

items.notes: Subject: history. Key letter C. Negated frame (could hardly be considered), in the manner of 2.21. One reversal (arduous, a natural word for the trip that the negation flips) and two unsupported words. Words avoided as options because they would be true under the negation: unprecedented (one woman had been before), leisurely. Raw freq.txt ranks: arduous 14,154; lucrative 23,461; routine 6,712; ceremonial 12,754.

items.passage: In 1993, artist Rick Lowe and collaborators began restoring dilapidated shotgun houses in Houston’s Third Ward neighborhood. Their organization, Project Row Houses, treats artistic practice as ______ community life: several houses serve as studios for visiting artists, while others give young single mothers a year of housing as they complete their education.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Inseparable from means joined so closely that the two cannot be pulled apart. The colon clause shows art and community support side by side in the same row of houses: “several houses serve as studios for visiting artists, while others give young single mothers a year of housing.”

A.why_wrong: Detached from means separate from. The organization puts artists’ studios in the same row as housing for young mothers, so it joins art and community life rather than keeping them apart.

C.why_wrong: Modeled on means patterned after. Nothing suggests that the art made in the studios copies community life; the text shows the two placed together.

D.why_wrong: Subordinate to means ranked below. The text gives the studios and the housing program equal place in the houses and never ranks one beneath the other.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Project Row Houses: founded 1993 by Rick Lowe and six other artists in Houston's Third Ward; restored shotgun houses in poor condition; eight houses serve as studios for visiting artists; Young Mothers Residential Program gives single mothers one year of housing while they complete their education

items.notes: Subject: humanities (art, community practice). Key letter B. Example clue after a colon, adjective + preposition options as in 2.28. One reversal, one unsupported, one near miss (subordinate to). Raw freq.txt ranks: detached from 7,786; inseparable from 12,724; modeled on 3,427; subordinate to 13,590.

items.passage: Enslaved potter David Drake signed and dated many large stoneware storage jars he made in Edgefield, South Carolina, and inscribed several with rhyming couplets. Scholars have characterized these inscriptions as acts of ______: by writing on his pottery, Drake openly did exactly what the state’s prohibitions on teaching enslaved people to write were specifically intended to prevent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Defiance is open refusal to obey. The colon clause says that by writing on his pottery Drake “openly did exactly what the state’s prohibitions on teaching enslaved people to write were specifically intended to prevent,” which is exactly an act of defiance.

A.why_wrong: Deference means respectful submission. Drake did what the prohibitions were meant to prevent, so his inscriptions were the opposite of submission.

B.why_wrong: Ingenuity means cleverness. Drake may well have been clever, but the colon clause explains the inscriptions by their relation to the law, not by their cleverness.

C.why_wrong: Nostalgia means longing for the past. Nothing in the text concerns memory or longing; it concerns writing that the law sought to stop.

sources.what: Wikipedia, David Drake (potter): enslaved potter in Edgefield, South Carolina; signed and dated large alkaline-glazed stoneware and added verses, usually rhyming couplets; South Carolina law barred teaching enslaved people to read and write; some scholars see his inscriptions as an act of defiance

items.notes: Subject: history and humanities (craft). Key letter D. Restatement after a colon. One reversal, one near miss, one unsupported. Raw freq.txt ranks: deference 5,568; ingenuity 8,623; nostalgia 60,574; defiance 3,960.

items.passage: After a male cactus finch from the Galápagos island of Española arrived on Daphne Major, more than 100 kilometers away, and interbred with a resident medium ground finch, their descendants bred exclusively with one another from the second generation onward. Sangeet Lamichhaney and colleagues therefore concluded that this lineage had become ______ from the island’s other finches within three generations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Isolated means set apart. Because the pair’s descendants “bred exclusively with one another from the second generation onward,” they no longer mated with the island’s other finches, so the lineage was reproductively isolated from them.

B.why_wrong: Indistinguishable from means impossible to tell apart from. A lineage whose members mate only with one another has become separate from the other finches, not merged with them.

C.why_wrong: Dislodged from means forced out of a place. The text says nothing about the lineage being driven off Daphne Major; it describes whom its members bred with.

D.why_wrong: Exempt from means freed from a duty or rule. Nothing in the text concerns an obligation the finches were released from.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Lamichhaney et al. 2018 (Science), “Rapid hybrid speciation in Darwin's finches”: an immigrant G. conirostris male from Española, more than 100 kilometers away, bred with a resident G. fortis on Daphne Major; from the second generation onward the lineage bred endogamously; reproductive isolation established in only three generations

items.notes: Subject: natural science (evolution). Key letter A. Cause stated first, consequence signaled by therefore. One reversal and two unsupported words. Raw freq.txt ranks: isolated 7,655; indistinguishable 20,439; dislodged 22,457; exempt 19,409. Fame check: the passage names the specific 2018 lineage study, not Darwin's finches in general; “Darwin” is not used. G. conirostris is the Española cactus finch.

items.passage: On Kawara’s Today series, initiated in 1966, is distinguished by its ______. Each of its nearly 3,000 paintings depicts nothing except the date on which it was executed, in simple white lettering on a monochrome background, and Kawara destroyed any canvas he could not complete on the day he began it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Rigor is strictness in following rules. The examples show fixed rules strictly kept: every painting “depicts nothing except the date on which it was executed,” always in the same plain style, and Kawara “destroyed any canvas he could not complete on the day he began it.”

A.why_wrong: Extravagance means lavish excess. Paintings that show only a date “in simple white lettering on a monochrome background” are the opposite of lavish.

B.why_wrong: Ambiguity means openness to more than one meaning. Each painting states one thing plainly, the date it was made, so the examples do not show ambiguity.

D.why_wrong: Collaboration means working with others. The text mentions only Kawara making and destroying the paintings.

sources.what: Wikipedia, On Kawara: Japanese conceptual artist; Today series begun January 4, 1966; nearly 3,000 paintings; each consists entirely of the date on which it was executed in simple white lettering on a solid background; if he could not finish a painting on the day he started it, he destroyed it

items.notes: Subject: humanities (art). Key letter C. Example-pinned: the abstract quality the rules instantiate. Raw freq.txt ranks: extravagance 8,211; ambiguity 37,559; rigor 31,023; collaboration 19,073. “Spontaneity” was avoided as an option because one-day painting could be argued to be spontaneous.

items.passage: Since the 1990s, Chinese artist Cai Guo-Qiang has created artworks using an unconventional ______: gunpowder. He has incorporated it into drawings and has even arranged it on garments and ignited it, allowing the burning powder to imprint images into the fabric.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A material is the substance something is made from. The text names gunpowder and says Cai “has incorporated it into drawings” and burned it on garments “to imprint images into the fabric,” so gunpowder is a material for his art.

A.why_wrong: An audience is a group of people watching. Gunpowder is not a group of viewers; the text describes Cai making images with it.

C.why_wrong: An assistant is a person who helps. Gunpowder is a substance Cai works with, not a helper.

D.why_wrong: A title is the name of a work. The text does not say any work is named “gunpowder”; it describes how he uses the powder.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Cai Guo-Qiang: began exploring gunpowder in his drawings around 1995, leading to explosion events; for a 1998 Issey Miyake collaboration he arranged gunpowder on garments and set fire to it to burn the images into the clothes

items.notes: Subject: humanities (art). Key letter B. Restatement after a colon. Raw freq.txt ranks: audience 2,558; material 2,422; assistant 6,794; title 2,358. The Sky Ladder work (topic fame) is left out.

items.passage: The Australian stinging tree Dendrocnide moroides is known for the ______ pain caused by the tiny hairs covering its leaves and stems. A sting brings an intense burning sensation that usually lasts from hours to days, and some victims have reported suffering for weeks or even months afterward.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Prolonged means lasting a long time. The text says the burning “usually lasts from hours to days” and that “some victims have reported suffering for weeks or even months afterward,” so the pain the tree causes is prolonged.

A.why_wrong: Mild means slight or gentle. The text describes “an intense burning sensation,” so the pain is not mild.

B.why_wrong: Contagious means able to spread from one person to another. Nothing in the text says the pain passes between people; it describes how long the pain lasts.

C.why_wrong: Imaginary means not real. The text describes a real “intense burning sensation” caused by the plant’s hairs, not pain that victims imagine.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Dendrocnide moroides: Australian stinging tree; stem, branches, leaves and fruits covered in stinging hairs; notorious for an extremely painful sting which may leave victims suffering for weeks or even months; immediate severe burning that lasts from hours to several days before subsiding

items.notes: Reviewer replacement (lead: topic spread; the Sklarek item shared a “first African American woman” frame with item 15). Subject: natural science (botany). Key letter D. Restatement in the next sentence (lasts from hours to days, weeks or even months). One reversal (mild) and two unsupported words. Raw freq.txt ranks: mild 3,436; contagious 17,076; imaginary 6,384; prolonged 5,313. The 2020 toxin study (gympietides) is left out; the item rests on the duration of the pain only.

fixes: replaced at the lead’s request (topic spread; shared “first African American” frame with item 15): Norma Merrick Sklarek swapped for the Australian stinging tree, same cell (B1 easy, key D), sourced from Wikipedia, Dendrocnide moroides; claim appended, old one withdrawn

items.passage: Travel writer Eliza Scidmore was remarkably ______ in her campaign to bring Japanese cherry trees to Washington, DC. She first proposed planting them in the 1880s, and although park administrators expressed no interest for more than two decades, she continued advocating for the idea until First Lady Helen Taft embraced it in 1909.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Persistent means continuing firmly in spite of difficulty. The text says administrators “expressed no interest for more than two decades,” yet Scidmore “continued advocating for the idea” until it was taken up.

B.why_wrong: Hesitant means unsure and slow to act. Scidmore kept advocating for her idea for more than twenty years, which is the opposite of hesitating.

C.why_wrong: Careless means not paying attention. Nothing in the text suggests carelessness; it describes a long, determined campaign.

D.why_wrong: Wealthy means rich. The text says nothing about Scidmore’s money; it describes how long she kept up her campaign.

items.passage: From the 1950s onward, Brazilian artist Rubem Valentim produced paintings that were thoroughly ______: in them, emblems of the orishas (deities) worshipped in Candomblé, an Afro-Brazilian religion, such as Shango’s double-bladed axe and Oshosi’s arrow, are rendered in the vocabulary of geometric abstraction, an artistic idiom that originated in Europe and that Valentim adopted in those same years.
